chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'If a man tires during the Tawaf, is it permissible for him to rest?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, he may rest, then stand and continue building upon his Tawaf, whether in an obligatory one or another; and he may do that in his Sa'i and in all of his rituals.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim gets tired during Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that fatigue does not invalidate the ritual, allowing the pilgrim to pause and resume from the exact point of interruption, a principle known as *ibtida'* from the last completed unit. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on ease (*taysir*) and the continuity of worship, applying equally to Tawaf, Sa'i, and other pillars of Hajj. It reflects the broader theological view that divine commands are tailored to human capacity, preventing undue hardship in acts of devotion.
